author: pilot_suggester

checks.description: Reject unverified context, unsafe mount aliases/media and competing operations.
Complete actual GTK/provider/export workflow with real disposable mounts and preserved data.
Stage provider consistently and keep invalid-context entry points diagnostic-only.
Validate actual recovery context, removable media and physical input/failure behavior.

constraints.text: Bind trusted configuration to the actual running recovery root, mount namespace, mounted source/destination and kernel block ancestry. A marker, configured context string, filesystem label, raw device name or major:minor pair alone is insufficient. Refuse unknown or ambiguous topology, unexpected aliases/submounts, non-removable destinations, and any destination sharing an underlying system/source medium. Include negative tests for an ordinary A/B or workstation root carrying an apparent recovery marker and for unsupported storage stacks.

Require read-only source mount and filesystem-superblock state; reject a read-only bind view backed by a writable filesystem. Establish the recovery environment's source-writer and mount-namespace assumptions explicitly, and refuse when they cannot be verified. Document preservation requirements for premount preparation, including ext4 journal replay; the provider must not mount, repair, replay journals, change block flags or quiesce hardware as a fallback. Test writable backing aliases and inconsistent mount/superblock options.

Use one trusted admission protocol shared by all participating export/media mutators, with exclusive ownership held through writing, verification, publication and directory fsync. An otherwise unused lock is not evidence of system-wide exclusion. Bind mount and medium identity into the reviewed fingerprint, accounting for device-number reuse; recheck under admission before writing and before publication. Test competing processes, media replacement between review/apply, and disappearance or identity change during execution; failure must not publish a completed archive and must release the lease.

Exercise the actual GTK chooser, review, cancellation and apply path through the provider using real disposable read-only source and FAT mounts. Verify a damaged registry remains exportable, source contents and pre-existing destination files remain unchanged, and cancellation creates no archive. Fixture exceptions may identify explicitly marked disposable roots/loop media, but must not bypass shared validation/lease logic or be accepted by the production entry point. Mock mount tables alone do not satisfy this check.

Stage the provider with the matching runtime, reject missing/mismatched runtime sources, and keep absent, malformed, untrusted or invalid production context diagnostic-only with a useful reason. Ship no guessed target identities or automatically enabled export context. Record package/dependency and payload-size changes; keep complete 512 MiB recovery closure and 8 GB image-capacity acceptance open. Preserve the canonical human checklist for reviewed recovery boot, actual media removal/input/failure testing and named-profile evidence; no offline result may satisfy physical acceptance.

decision.rationale: This completes a bounded part of accepted decision 0010 without changing owner requirements. runtime/sv08_recovery_ui.py currently constructs its installed controller without an adapter, while runtime/sv08_export.py and docs/hardware/host-recovery-export.md establish reusable export behavior. The improvement is a reachable configured selection/review/export workflow with verified admission. However, tests/recovery_export_mounts.py checks only a read-only bind mount and a vfat destination; that does not establish filesystem-level quiescence, recovery identity or physical-media separation. Approval therefore requires the identity, exclusion and preservation checks below. Physical recovery-system integration remains blocked, the test printer's host PCB revision remains unknown, and this decision grants no hardware authority.

tasks.blocker: Reviewed the complete base-to-e54d46c diff and confirmed clean HEAD, submitted source/document hashes, approval hashes, unchanged indexed gitlinks, JSON/Markdown checks, and reported payload measurements. Independently passed all 40 targeted tests and four actual staged non-fixture GTK diagnostic cases. Material admission failure remains at runtime/sv08_recovery_media.py:230: normalizing wwid and device/wwid into one dictionary silently discards an identity. same_identity({'wwid':'known-system-medium','device/wwid':'other-value'}, {'wwid':'known-system-medium'}) returns false. Either alias ordering can lose the known match when the conflicting value occurs last. Reproduced through the production snapshot positive-control harness: adding these conflicting destination attributes allowed a known unmounted system medium; the expected refusal was not raised. This violates the approved requirement to reject system/source media and ambiguous topology. Retain all normalized identity values or refuse conflicting aliases, with regression tests covering both insertion orders and the full production snapshot. Physical recovery, named-profile validation, independent image/preparer integration, 512 MiB recovery closure and 8 GB capacity remain open.
